extracted.intended_audience: Associated Press journalists, editors and newsroom staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for reporting, editing and producing AP news across text, audio, video, photos, graphics and data, covering sourcing, attribution, corrections, privacy and multimedia handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio accuracy and non-manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: AP’s audio content always must be accurate. We do not alter or manipulate newsmaker actuality in any way, except as provided below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: with manager permission, shorten overly long pauses; subtle standard audio processing (normalization, general volume adjustments, equalization, noise reduction) and fading in/out start/end of sound bites — provided these methods do not conceal, obscure, remove or otherwise alter the content or any portion of the content. Bleeping allowed with manager permission to cover obscenities when necessary. Do not use sound effects or substitute audio from another event. Consult desk supervisor / senior editor with questions or before transmission when in doubt. Voice reports may be edited to remove pauses or stumbles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio & video editing must not alter meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The video or audio editing of quotations or soundbites must not alter the speaker’s meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal editing of audio soundbites of newsmakers is not permitted. Shortened soundbites by cutaway or video transition are permitted only if the speaker’s meaning is not altered or misconstrued. Sound edits for technical failures may be allowed only after approval by a senior editorial manager. When music is principal ambient sound in contemporaneous video, audio may be laid unbroken and images edited over provided meaning is not altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphics: authoritative sourcing and no speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: We use only authoritative sources. We do not project, surmise or estimate in a graphic. We create work only from what we know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use graphics provided by others unless underlying data is available (except when authorized by a manager). Create charts with visually proper perspectives to accurately represent data. Credit sources on every interactive and graphic, including those using AP-created databases. Information must be clear and concise; do not skew or alter data to fit a visual need.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charting resolution and axis rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Line charts are great for tracking trends; bar charts compare data points and must not distort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line charts: value axis does not have to start at zero but chart should be balanced within the middle and must not omit time periods; keep time intervals even. Bar charts: value axis must always start at zero to avoid inaccurate conclusions and exaggerated data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo accuracy and limits on image editing
rubrics_metrics.description: AP images must always be accurate. We do not alter or digitally manipulate the content of a photo or video except as stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor adjustments acceptable: cropping, dodging and burning, conversion to grayscale, elimination of dust/scratches on scans, normal toning and color adjustments — limited to what is minimally necessary to restore/clarify the authentic nature of the photograph. Changes that substantially alter the original scene (density, contrast, color, saturation) are not acceptable. Backgrounds should not be digitally blurred or eliminated by aggressive toning. Removal of 'red eye' is not permissible. Employees with questions should contact a senior photo editor prior to transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video technical improvements allowed but content must remain accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: For video, AP permits subtle, standard methods of improving technical quality provided they do not conceal, obscure, remove or otherwise alter the content of the image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: adjusting video and audio levels, color correcting due to white balance, eliminating buzzing/hums/clicks/pops or overly long pauses, equalization to improve clarity. Video can be produced with titles and logos, toning and audio improvements. When editing audio within video, generally use the specific audio associated with each shot without alteration; exceptions for music-based ambient sound when contemporaneous and meaning not altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo-based graphics must not misrepresent and must be clearly graphics
rubrics_metrics.description: Composed photo-based graphics (e.g., headshot layered with a logo) must not misrepresent the facts and must not look like a photograph — it must clearly be a graphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When altering photos to use as graphics online, retain integrity of the image and limit changes to cropping, masking and adding elements like logos. It is permissible to display photos online with techniques (360-degree panoramas, dissolves) as long as original images are not altered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of others' material and anti-plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: AP staffers must use original content, language and phrasing and must not plagiarize others’ work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short passages from previous AP stories (background/boilerplate) are acceptable if short and the reporter remains responsible for factual/contextual accuracy. AP often has rights to members’ and subscribers’ material and must credit them. Do not publish news releases in original form; you may use info, quotes and properly cleared images from releases but must judge credibility, augment with other sources, and prepare your own story with credit. For video, name other broadcasters on shotlists and credit pickups of audio/graphics when requested by the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-of-reply and responses to subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must make significant efforts to reach anyone who may be portrayed negatively and give them a reasonable amount of time to respond before sending reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is 'reasonable' depends on urgency/competitiveness. If parties cannot be reached, explain in the story what efforts were made. Seek comment and balance when reporting allegations or negative portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous sources: strict conditions and managerial approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Material from anonymous sources may be used only under strict guidelines enforced by AP news managers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anonymous material only if: it is information (not opinion/speculation) vital to the report; not available except under anonymity; the source is reliable and has direct knowledge. Reporters must get manager approval before sending the story; managers must know the source identity and vet the material while keeping it confidential. Seek more than one source where possible; rarely one authoritative source may suffice. Explain in the story why anonymity was requested and, when relevant, the source’s motive. Describe how documents were obtained if story hinges on them. Attribution must establish credibility (avoid vague 'a source'). Stories using anonymous sources must carry a reporter’s byline; contributing reporters who provide anonymous material should be credited as contributors. Complaints about authenticity must be brought to the manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: on the record / off the record / background / deep background
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent definitions must be used to set ground rules with sources regarding attribution and use of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the record: information may be used quoting the source by name. Off the record: information cannot be used for publication. Background: information can be published under negotiated conditions, usually without the name but with a descriptive attribution. Deep background: information can be used only without attribution in any form. Before interviews expecting any anonymity, set ground rules explicitly. Information obtained under these conditions can be pursued with other sources to place it on the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutiny of anonymous material from other outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous-source material from other news organizations requires careful scrutiny before pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AP’s anonymous-source rules apply equally to material from other outlets: material must be factual and unobtainable any other way; story must be significant; use must be authorized by a manager; make bona fide effort to get it on the record or confirm via own reporting; attribute to originating news organization and note its description of the source if used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of disputable material
rubrics_metrics.description: Anything in AP news reports that could reasonably be disputed should be attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full name and identifying information (age, title, organization, hometown) as needed to establish credibility. Identify quotations taken from documents (reports, emails, releases). Internet-sourced information must be vetted and attributed to the original source. File/library/archive photos, audio or videos must be identified as such. For lengthy stories, use an extended editor’s note detailing interviews, research and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotations must be used accurately and in context
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes must not be taken out of context; we do not alter or manipulate quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter quotations even to correct grammar; if flawed, paraphrase only if completely true to the original; if too murky to paraphrase accurately, do not use. Ellipses should be rare and must not alter meaning. When relevant, provide the setting in which a quotation was obtained and note source’s affect or body language. Limit nonstandard spellings of dialects; translate quotes faithfully and note language spoken when appropriate. Internal editing of audio soundbites is not permitted; shortened soundbites allowed only if meaning unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A dateline tells the reader where basic information for a story was obtained; for multimedia it must reflect where events depicted occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For short routine un-by-lined stories, dateline should reflect where story took place. For longer or analytical stories or those with multiple elements, dateline should be where the staffer covering the story is located. If supplementary info is obtained elsewhere, note it in the story. For video/photos/audio, dateline must be where events depicted actually occurred. For voice work, dateline must be location from which reporter is speaking; if not possible, do not use a dateline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and crediting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines tell who wrote the story and should reflect contribution and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For text stories with datelines, bylines used only if journalist was in the datelined location. If multiple staffers contributed substantially, use editor’s judgment for single or double bylines; indicate who was where in an end note if needed. Give bylines to photographers, broadcast reporters and video journalists who provide information without which there would be no story. For roundups, byline goes to the writer with contributor credit in an editor’s note. Do not use pseudonyms/"air names" for staffers unless approved by a manager.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and corrective practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Staffers must notify supervisory editors as soon as possible of serious errors or potential errors and correct mistakes promptly and transparently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When wrong, say so as soon as possible. Corrections must be labeled 'correction' — do not use euphemisms. Notify subscriber editors and make corrections visible to news consumers (bottom-of-story corrections, correction notes on graphics, photo captions, etc.). For live broadcasts, correct in same newscast if possible or next appropriate live segment. For online/live text stories, overwrite previous version and send separate corrective stories as warranted. Graphics corrections should carry a FIX logo/bug. Photo caption corrections should be retransmitted with corrected caption and marked as retransmission to correct an error. Video corrections: scripts/shotlists sent to clients as advisories and labeled as such. Audio: eliminate audio correspondent reports with factual errors and replace with corrected reports when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No fabrication or staging
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in AP news reports — words, photos, graphics, sound or video — may be fabricated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use pseudonyms (except established literary names/noms de guerre which must be identified), composite characters, fictional names, ages, places or dates. Do not stage or re-enact events for camera/microphone. Do not add sound effects or substitute video/audio from another event to embellish or fabricate an event. Virtual reality presentations must consist of real, unmanipulated imagery and sound. Consult senior editor before introducing any neutral sound that affects editorial meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for victims and minors
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect the identities of victims of sexual assault, extreme abuse and minors in many circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally do not identify people who say they have been sexually assaulted or subjected to extreme abuse; may identify victims when they publicly identify themselves. Generally do not identify minors accused of crimes or who are witnesses; identification must be approved by a manager and may depend on severity, formal charging, public safety (e.g., manhunt) or de facto public knowledge. Consider public safety and other factors when deciding on identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling obscenities, profanities and hate material
rubrics_metrics.description: AP resists serving as a conduit for hate or propaganda and limits use of offensive language and imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hate speech or images are central, briefly refer to them rather than carrying them at length. Senior manager must vet material showing hostages or kidnappers’ statements; quote minimally and note duress. Do not use obscenities, racial epithets or offensive slurs unless part of direct quotations and there is a compelling reason; do not run imagery of such slurs without manager consultation. If a story cannot be told without slurs, try to convey sense without using the specific word; if used, flag content at top to advise editors/clients. Tailor advisories and selection of video/audio according to platform/customer. Do not link directly to obscene/offensive websites; link the least offensive image necessary to tell the story. Photos containing potentially offensive content must carry an editor’s note flagging it; video/audio containing offensive material must be flagged in rundowns/billboards/scripts for clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credits for use of other organizations’ broadcast material
rubrics_metrics.description: When using another broadcaster’s material, provide appropriate credit and documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For video, advise the name of the broadcaster on the accompanying shotlist. Pickups of audio and television graphics are credited in billboards/captions when the source requests it. Attribute material from other outlets and indicate their description of anonymous sources when used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: AP employees must avoid behavior or activities that create conflicts of interest or compromise the ability to report news accurately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff should not engage in outside activities or behavior that could influence or appear to influence editorial judgment; disclose and seek guidance/approval when potential conflicts arise.
